comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 adopted programme appendix governs the 60-EC compulsory first year and the shared second/third-year units. The generic bachelor offers Pedagogy/Educational Sciences and Orthopedagogy; the former is chosen as the broad upbringing-and-education route, not for UCR fit. A coherent 180 EC consists of 60 first-year EC, 50 individually listed common upper-year EC, 25 route EC, two explicitly permitted 2.5-EC research workshops, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC genuine minor choice. The appendix labels the common part 55 EC and the differentiated part 25 EC, although its individually listed common units total 50 EC and the route units plus workshops total 30 EC. The individually specified units and the 90-EC major total reconcile when the workshops are included; this grouping discrepancy is recorded rather than inventing an unnamed five-credit course. The general prospectus still displays older first-year course titles, so the current appendix governs the 2026–27 component identities.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic 180-EC Pedagogical Sciences target does not name a route. The 2026–27 appendix offers Pedagogy/Educational Sciences and Orthopedagogy; the former broadly retains upbringing, education, family, social development and educational policy, whereas the latter is more specialised in diagnostics and intervention. The four-year primary-school teacher double degree is not the ordinary bachelor route. This choice precedes UCR course selection.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The brain-and-behaviour foundation precedes its formally dependent psychology and cognition courses, and research/statistics precede organisational psychology. Introductory sociology and rhetoric precede their advanced applications where schedules permit. Every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term; 24 unique courses include nine 300-level courses and first-year PPD.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest UCR programme uses the available developmental, cognitive, sociological and research curriculum without claiming specialist pedagogy. The orthopedagogy candidate cannot support a second child-specific clinical and intervention sequence, and the teacher-education candidate requires professional classroom training and a second degree that UCR does not offer. A further alternative is therefore not constructed.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine developmental psychology; UCR spans the whole lifespan rather than a pedagogical context.
Both address neurobiological foundations of cognition and behaviour; UCR is a general neurobiology course.
Both examine social development and relationships; UCR social psychology has broader age coverage.
Both address behavioural difficulties; UCR offers general abnormal psychology rather than orthopedagogy.
Both examine psychological measurement and assessment; Groningen test theory is a dedicated psychometric unit while UCR embeds it in clinical assessment.
UCR has developmental study but no specific course on early-childhood perspectives and policy.
Both examine the social organisation of education and inequality; UCR is a wider introduction to sociology.
Both study organisational processes and professional learning; UCR covers general organisational psychology rather than educational institutions specifically.
UCR has no dedicated history of upbringing and education.
UCR lacks a foundational pedagogy course.
UCR lacks a theoretical pedagogy course.
UCR offers child development and school-linked rhetoric but no introduction to educational science.
No UCR course specifically teaches intercultural pedagogy.
UCR social and developmental courses do not constitute family pedagogy.
The Groningen unit evaluates effectiveness of education; UCR has no comparable instructional-effectiveness course.
This 30-EC space is a genuine student choice among permitted minors, not a compulsory specialist subject.
Both introduce empirical research questions, design and interpretation.
Both introduce qualitative social-science research and analysis.
Both teach quantitative research design and statistical inference; UCR emphasises experiments.
Both critically synthesise published research through systematic review; UCR additionally teaches meta-analysis.
The Groningen unit is a separate, discipline-specific qualitative methods requirement.
The Groningen designs practicum includes an integrated programme-specific research assignment and learning community.
Statistical Models 2 is a further required statistics unit beyond the UCR course already matched.
UCR has qualitative methods but no separately credited interview and content-analysis workshop in this programme.
Groningen requires a 10-EC pedagogical bachelor thesis; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only.
Both explicitly develop academic reflection and professional orientation, though Groningen uses programme-specific learning communities.
Both consider law and social responsibility; UCR surveys legal fields rather than Dutch education law.
General UCR ethics does not reproduce philosophy specifically for pedagogues.
UCR rhetoric is public speaking rather than supervised professional conversation practice.
UCR does not offer Groningen’s programme-specific bachelor internship.
UCR has ethics but no separately credited philosophy-of-science unit in this curriculum.

notes.text: Groningen requires a dedicated sequence in pedagogy and educational sciences, programme-specific research workshops, a bachelor internship and a thesis. UCR can combine developmental psychology, cognition, sociology, communication and research, but does not reproduce the specialist pedagogical curriculum or professional practice route.
